cards.description: Rhododendron ponticum, called common rhododendron or pontic rhododendron, is a species of flowering plant in the heath family Ericaceae. It is native to the Iberian Peninsula in southwest Europe and the Caucasus region in northern West Asia.
cards.keyFeatures: R. ponticum is a dense, suckering shrub or small tree growing to 5 m (16 ft) tall, rarely 8 m (26 ft). The leaves are evergreen, 6 to 18 cm (2.4 to 7.1 in) long and 2 to 5 cm (0.79 to 1.97 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rafael Medina, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Mountain Hickory Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia obliquinervia
cards.description: Acacia obliquinervia, known colloquially as mountain hickory or mountain hickory wattle, is a species of Acacia that is endemic to southeastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The shrub or tree can grow to a height of 1 to 15 m (3 ft 3 in to 49 ft 3 in) and can have an erect or spreading habit. The has dark brown coloured and deeply fissured bark with angled or flattened and glabrous branchlets that are often covered in a fine white powdery coating.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leon Perrie, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Chinese Fringe Flower
cards.subtitle: Loropetalum chinense
cards.description: Loropetalum chinense, commonly known as loropetalum, Chinese fringe flower and strap flower is a shrub or small tree in the witch-hazel family, Hamamelidaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: They are evergreen with branches forming horizontal layers. The leaves are alternately arranged, ovate 2.5 to 5 cm (1 to 2 in) long by 2.5 cm (1 in) wide, and have a slightly abrasive feel.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Amanda Rose Ross, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Amanda Rose Ross

cards.name: Wollemi Pine
cards.subtitle: Wollemia nobilis
cards.description: Wollemia nobilis is a species of coniferous tree in the family Araucariaceae. It is the single known species in the monotypic genus Wollemia. The species represents one of only three living genera in the family, alongside Araucaria and Agathis (being more closely related to the latter), which was discovered in 1994 in a temperate rainforest wilderness area of the Wollemi National Park in New South Wales.
cards.keyFeatures: Wollemia nobilis is an evergreen tree reaching 25–40 m (82–131 ft) tall. The bark is very distinctive, dark brown, and knobbly, quoted as resembling the breakfast cereal Coco Pops.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Grzegorz Grzejszczak, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Grzegorz Grzejszczak

cards.name: Ovens Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia pravissima
cards.description: Acacia pravissima, commonly known as Ovens wattle, Oven wattle, wedge-leaved wattle and Tumut wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the legume family, Fabaceae. It is an evergreen shrub native to southeastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The tree or shrub typically grows to a height of 0.5 to 3 metres (1+1⁄2 to 10 ft) but can grow as tall as 8 m (26 ft) and has slender to spreading branches. The ribbed branchlets can be either glabrous or hairy.
cards.imageCredit: (c) ttsquid, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Tree Mallow
cards.subtitle: Malva arborea
cards.description: Malva arborea (previously known as Lavatera arborea, or, more recently as Malva eriocalyx), the tree mallow, is a species of mallow native to the coasts of western Europe and the Mediterranean region, from Ireland and Britain south to Algeria and Libya, and east to Greece.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a shrubby annual, biennial or perennial plant growing to 0.5–2 m (rarely 3 m) tall. The leaves are orbicular, 8–18 cm diameter, palmately lobed with five to nine lobes, and a coarsely serrated margin.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cricket Raspet, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cricket Raspet

cards.name: Austral Grass-tree
cards.subtitle: Xanthorrhoea australis
cards.description: Xanthorrhoea australis, the grass tree or austral grasstree, is an Australian plant. It is the most commonly seen species of the genus Xanthorrhoea. Its trunk can grow up to several metres tall and is often branched.
cards.keyFeatures: The main way to identify Xanthorrhoea is by looking at the cross-section of the leaves. In the case of X. australis the cross-section is a rough diamond shape, and the colour of the leaves is a bluish-green.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Grey Box
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus microcarpa
cards.description: Eucalyptus microcarpa, commonly known as grey box, is a species of tree that is endemic to southeastern continental Australia. It has rough, fibrous or flaky bark on the trunk, smooth whitish bark above, lance-shaped adult leaves, flower buds in groups of between seven and eleven, white flowers and oval, cylindrical or urn-shaped fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus microcarpa is a spreading tree, sometimes with several trunks, that typically grows to a height of 25 m (82 ft) and forms a lignotuber. It has rough, fibrous or flaky bark on the trunk as far as the larger branches, smooth greyish or whitish bark above.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sid Miller, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Round Leaf Box
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus baueriana
cards.description: Eucalyptus baueriana, commonly known as blue box or round-leaved box, is a tree that is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has rough, fibrous or flaky bark on the trunk and branches, egg-shaped adult leaves, oval to diamond-shaped flower buds arranged in groups of seven, white flowers and conical fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus baueriana is a tree that grows to a height of about 20 metres (66 ft), sometimes a small tree or mallee to 12 metres (39 ft) high, and forms a lignotuber. It has persistent, light grey, fibrous or flaky bark with whitish patches, on the trunk and larger branches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terra Occ

cards.name: Cherry-plum
cards.subtitle: Prunus cerasifera
cards.description: Prunus cerasifera is a species of plum known by the common names cherry plum and myrobalan plum. Native to Eurasia and naturalized elsewhere, P. cerasifera is believed to be one of the parents of the cultivated plum.
cards.keyFeatures: Wild types are large shrubs or small trees reaching 8–12 metres (26–39 ft) tall, sometimes spiny, with glabrous, ovate deciduous leaves 3–7 cm (1–3 in) long. It is one of the first European trees to flower in spring, often starting in mid-February before the leaves have opened.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Maja Dumat, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Norfolk Island Pine
cards.subtitle: Araucaria heterophylla
cards.description: Araucaria heterophylla (synonym A. excelsa) is a species of conifer. As its vernacular name Norfolk Island pine (or Norfolk pine) implies, the tree is endemic to Norfolk Island, an external territory of Australia located in the Pacific Ocean between New Zealand and New Caledonia.
cards.keyFeatures: The tree is slow growing and can reach a height of 50–65 m (160–210 ft), with straight vertical trunks and symmetrical branches, even in the face of incessant onshore winds that can contort most other species. From the straight trunk, it emits five almost horizontal or slightly oblique branches, forming floors; the plane of each floor is a perfect pentagon.
cards.imageCredit: (c) bertknot, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Victorian Silver Gum
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus crenulata
cards.description: Eucalyptus crenulata, commonly known as Buxton gum, silver gum or Victorian silver gum, is a rare species of medium-sized tree that is found only in the wild in a small area in Victoria but is widely planted. It has rough, compacted bark on the trunk, sessile, egg-shaped to heart-shaped leaves arranged in opposite pairs, flower buds covered with a white, powdery bloom, white flowers and cup-shaped fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus crenulata is a tree that typically grows to a height of 10–12 m (30–40 ft) and forms a lignotuber. It has hard, rough, compacted, grey to brown or black bark on the trunk and smooth grey or yellowish bark on the branches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Melburnian, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: New Zealand Cabbage Tree
cards.subtitle: Cordyline australis
cards.description: Cordyline australis, commonly known as the cabbage tree, or by its Māori name of tī or tī kōuka, is a widely branched monocot tree endemic to New Zealand. It grows up to 20 metres (66 feet) tall with a stout trunk and sword-like leaves, which are clustered at the tips of the branches and can be up to 1 metre (3 feet 3 inches) long.
cards.keyFeatures: Cordyline australis grows up to 20 metres (66 feet) tall with a stout trunk 1.5 to 2 m (4 ft 11 in to 6 ft 7 in) in diameter. The largest known tree, at Pākawau, Golden Bay / Mohua, was estimated to be 400 or 500 years old, and stood 17 metres (56 feet) tall with a circumference of 9 metres (30 feet) at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sandy Austin, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Varnish Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia verniciflua
cards.description: Acacia verniciflua, commonly known as varnish wattle, is a shrub or small tree species that is endemic to Australia. The species occurs in dry sclerophyll forest in South Australia, Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland. It is often found growing alongside Eucalyptus obliqua where it can dominate the understory.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Smooth-barked Apple
cards.subtitle: Angophora costata
cards.description: Angophora costata, commonly known as Sydney red gum, rusty gum or smooth-barked apple, is a species of tree that is endemic to eastern Australia. Reaching 30 m (100 ft) in height, the species has distinctive smooth bark that is pinkish or orange-brown when new and fades to grey with age.
cards.keyFeatures: Angophora costata is a tree that typically grows to a height of 30 m (100 ft) and forms a lignotuber. It has smooth pinkish or orange-brown bark that weathers to grey and is shed in small scales.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Tess McGrigor

cards.name: Strawberry Tree
cards.subtitle: Arbutus unedo
cards.description: Arbutus unedo, commonly known as strawberry-tree, or strawberry tree, also called madroño in Spanish, is an evergreen shrub or small tree in the family Ericaceae, native to the Mediterranean Basin and Western Europe. The tree is well known for its fruit, the arbutus berry, which bears some resemblance to the strawberry, hence the common name strawberry-tree.
cards.keyFeatures: Arbutus unedo grows to 4–7 m (13–23 ft) tall, rarely up to 13 m (45 ft), with a trunk diameter of up to 120 cm (47 in). It grows in hardiness zones 7–10.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Duarte Frade, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Duarte Frade

cards.name: Callery Pear
cards.subtitle: Pyrus calleryana
cards.description: Pyrus calleryana, also known as the Callery pear, is a species of pear tree native to East Asia in the family Rosaceae. Its cultivar Bradford pear, known for its offensive odor that some have described as akin to "rotting fish", is widely planted throughout the United States and increasingly regarded as an invasive species.
cards.keyFeatures: Pyrus calleryana is deciduous, growing to 5 to 8 m (16 to 26 ft) tall, often with a conical to rounded crown. The leaves are oval, 4 to 8 cm (1+1⁄2 to 3 in) long, glossy dark green above, and pale beneath.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Benjamin Smith, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: River Sheoak
cards.subtitle: Casuarina cunninghamiana
cards.description: Casuarina cunninghamiana, commonly known as river oak, river sheoak or creek oak, is a species of flowering plant in the family Casuarinaceae and is native to Australia and New Guinea. It is a tree with fissured and scaly bark, sometimes drooping branchlets, the leaves reduced to scales in whorls of 6 to 10, the fruit 7–14 mm (0.28–0.55 in) long containing winged seeds (samaras) 3–4 mm (0.12–0.16 in) long.
cards.keyFeatures: Casuarina cunninghamiana is a dioecious tree that typically grows to a height of 15–35 m (49–115 ft), has a DBH of 0.5–1.5 m (1 ft 8 in – 4 ft 11 in). Its bark is finely fissured, scaly and greyish brown.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jay Horn, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jay Horn

cards.name: Silver-leaved Mountain Gum
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus pulverulenta
cards.description: Eucalyptus pulverulenta, commonly known as silver-leaved mountain gum, is a species of straggly tree or mallee that is endemic to southern New South Wales. It has smooth bark, egg-shaped, heart-shaped or round, sessile leaves arranged in opposite pairs, flower buds in groups of three, white flowers and cup-shaped to cylindrical fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus pulverulenta is a straggly tree or mallee that typically grows to a height of 5 m (16 ft) or a tree to 9 m (30 ft), and forms a lignotuber. It has smooth, greenish to grey or brown bark, sometimes hanging in short ribbons.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Alfredo F. Fuentes Claros

cards.name: Old Man Banksia
cards.subtitle: Banksia serrata
cards.description: Banksia serrata, commonly known as the saw banksia, the old man banksia, the saw-tooth banksia or the red honeysuckle and as wiriyagan by the Cadigal people, is a species of woody shrub or tree of the genus Banksia, in the family Proteaceae. Native to the east coast of Australia, it is found from Queensland to Victoria with outlying populations on Tasmania and Flinders Island.
cards.keyFeatures: Banksia serrata usually grows as a gnarled and misshapen tree up to 16 m (50 ft) tall, although in some coastal habitats it grows as a shrub of 1–3 m (3–10 ft), and on exposed coastal cliffs it has even been recorded as a prostrate shrub. As a tree it usually has a single, stout trunk with warty, knobbly grey bark up to 3 cm (1.2 in) thick.
cards.imageCredit: (c) T. Hammer, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by T. Hammer

cards.name: Lemon-scented Gum
cards.subtitle: Corymbia citriodora
cards.description: Corymbia citriodora, commonly known as lemon-scented gum and other common names, is a species of tall tree that is endemic to north-eastern Australia. It has smooth white to pink bark, narrow lance-shaped to curved adult leaves, flower buds in groups of three, white flowers and urn-shaped or barrel-shaped fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Corymbia citriodora is a tree that typically grows to a height of 25–40 m (82–131 ft), sometimes to 50 m (160 ft) and forms a lignotuber. It has smooth, pale, uniform or slightly mottled, white to pink or coppery bark that is shed in thin flakes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Greg Tasney, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Greg Tasney

cards.name: Dwarf Apple
cards.subtitle: Angophora hispida
cards.description: Angophora hispida grows as a mallee, or as a tree to about 7 m (23 ft) in height. Its small size, especially when compared to its Angophora and Eucalyptus relatives, leads to it being known by the common name dwarf apple. It is native to a relatively small patch of central New South Wales – from just south of Sydney up to the Gosford area.
cards.keyFeatures: Dwarf apple grows as a small tree or mallee to 7 m (23 ft) high. It has greyish flaky bark.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Ginkgo
cards.subtitle: Ginkgo biloba
cards.description: Ginkgo biloba, commonly known as ginkgo ( GINK-oh, -⁠goh), also known as the maidenhair tree, and often misspelled "gingko" (see Taxonomy below) is a species of gymnosperm tree native to East Asia. It is the last living species in the order Ginkgoales, which first appeared over 290 million years ago.
cards.keyFeatures: Ginkgos have a conical crown in youth which becomes progressively broader and more irregular with age. They are large trees, normally reaching a height of 20–35 m (66–115 ft), with some specimens in China being over 40 m (130 ft).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Marco Mussita, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Marco Mussita

cards.name: Oriental Plane
cards.subtitle: Platanus orientalis
cards.description: Platanus orientalis, the Oriental plane, or chinar or booni (also boin), is a large, deciduous tree in the family Platanaceae, native from the eastern Mediterranean to Iran. It typically grows along rivers, streams and springs, and has broad spreading crown, exfoliating bark, deeply lobed leaves and pendent infructescences bearing spherical fruiting heads.
cards.keyFeatures: The oriental plane is found naturally in riverine settings, together with such trees as alder, willow and poplar. However, it is quite capable of survival and success in dry soils once it is established.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rosa-Maria Rinkl, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Cinnamon Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia leprosa
cards.description: Acacia leprosa, also known as cinnamon wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is an erect or spreading, sticky, aromatic shrub, occasionally a tree, elliptic or narrowly elliptic to lance-shaped phyllodes, usually two spherical heads of pale yellow flowers and thinly leathery to firmly papery pods.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia leprosa is an erect or spreading, sticky, aromatic shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–5 m (3 ft 3 in – 16 ft 5 in), occasionally a tree 8–10 m (26–33 ft), sometimes with more or less pendulous branches and glabrous, straight branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Strawberry Dogwood
cards.subtitle: Cornus capitata
cards.description: Cornus capitata is an Asian species of dogwood known by the common names Bentham's cornel, evergreen dogwood, Himalayan flowering dogwood, and Himalayan strawberry-tree.
cards.keyFeatures: This is an evergreen tree growing to 12 metres (39 feet) in height and width. The leaves are gray-green and pale and fuzzy underneath, and several centimetres long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leuba Ridgway, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Oleander
cards.subtitle: Nerium oleander
cards.description: Nerium oleander, the oleander, is a shrub or small tree native to the Mediterranean region east to southern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal east to India and Myanmar; the Flora of China also cites it as native in Yunnan in China. It is the only species currently classified in the genus Nerium, belonging to subfamily Apocynoideae of the dogbane family Apocynaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Oleander grows to 2–6 metres (7–20 feet) tall, with erect stems that splay outward as they mature; first-year stems have a glaucous bloom, while mature stems have a greyish bark. It is most commonly grown in its natural shrub form, but can be trained into a small tree with a single trunk.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Santiago Martín-Bravo, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Santiago Martín-Bravo

cards.name: Yarra Gum
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus yarraensis
cards.description: Eucalyptus yarraensis, commonly known as Yarra gum, is a tree species that is endemic to Victoria, Australia. It has rough bark on the trunk and larger branches, lance-shaped to elliptical or egg-shaped adult leaves, flower buds in groups of seven, white flowers and conical fruit. In 2021 the Victorian Government listed it as critically endangered under the Flora and Fauna Guarantee Act.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus yarraensis is a tree that typically grows to a height of 15–20 m (49–66 ft) and forms a lignotuber. It has rough, fibrous, brown or greyish bark on the trunk and larger branches, smooth white to cream-coloured bark above.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Chinese Arborvitae
cards.subtitle: Platycladus orientalis
cards.description: Platycladus is a monotypic genus of coniferous trees in the cypress family Cupressaceae, containing only one species, Platycladus orientalis, the Chinese thuja, Oriental arborvitae, Chinese arborvitae, biota or Oriental thuja. It is native to northeastern parts of East Asia and North Asia, but is also now naturalised as an introduced species in other regions of the Asian continent.
cards.keyFeatures: A monoecious tree, it is small, slow-growing, reaching 15–20 m (49–66 ft) and 3–5 m (9.8–16.4 ft) trunk diameter. The foliage forms in flat sprays with scale-like leaves 2–4 mm (0.08–0.16 in) long, which are bright green in colour but may turn brownish, yellow-green, or coppery orange in winter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Patrick Hacker, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Patrick Hacker

cards.name: Tasmanian Blue Gum
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus globulus
cards.description: Eucalyptus globulus, commonly known as southern blue gum, is a species of flowering plant in the family Myrtaceae. It is a tall, evergreen tree endemic to southeastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus globulus is a tree that typically grows to a height of 45 m (148 ft) but may sometimes only be a stunted shrub, or alternatively under ideal conditions can grow as tall as 90 m (300 ft), and forms a lignotuber. The bark is usually smooth, white to cream-coloured but there are sometimes slabs of persistent, unshed bark at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Forest and Kim Starr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Sasanqua Camellia
cards.subtitle: Camellia sasanqua
cards.description: Camellia sasanqua, with common name Sasanqua camellia or Christmas camellia (茶梅, サザンカ), is an evergreen shrub or small tree in the genus Camellia, section Oleifera of the family Theaceae. It is native to southern Japan (Shikoku, Kyushu) and the Ryukyu Islands. It has a long cultivation history in East Asia, used both as an ornamental plant and for seed oil extraction and leaf tea.
cards.keyFeatures: Camellia sasanqua is an evergreen shrub or small tree, usually reaching 6 m (20 ft) in height (wild specimens can reach 10 m (33 ft)). The leaves are alternate, leathery, elliptic to ovate, 2.6–6.3 cm (1.0–2.5 in) long and 0.9–3.2 cm (0.35–1.26 in) wide, with finely serrate margins.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Marco Mussita, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Marco Mussita

cards.name: Kōhūhū
cards.subtitle: Pittosporum tenuifolium
cards.description: Pittosporum tenuifolium is a small evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand – growing up to 10 m (33 ft) – commonly known as kōhūhū and black matipo, and by other Māori names kohukohu and tawhiwhi. Its small, very dark, reddish-purple flowers generally go unnoticed, and are scented only at night. The Latin tenuifolium means "slender-leaved".
cards.keyFeatures: Pittosporum translates to tarry – pittos – seed – sporum, a reference to the sticky fluid that encases the seeds and tenuifolium means thin – tenui – leaf – folium. Kōhūhū is a bush or small tree that grows up to around 8–10 metres tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) David Orlovich, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by David Orlovich

cards.name: Cherry Laurel
cards.subtitle: Prunus laurocerasus
cards.description: Prunus laurocerasus, also known as cherry laurel, common laurel and sometimes English laurel in North America, is an evergreen species of cherry (Prunus), native to regions bordering the Black Sea in southwestern Asia and southeastern Europe, from Albania and Bulgaria east through Turkey to the Caucasus Mountains and northern Iran.
cards.keyFeatures: Prunus laurocerasus is an evergreen shrub or small to medium-sized tree, growing to 5 to 15 metres (16 to 49 ft) tall, rarely to 18 metres (59 ft), with a trunk up to 60 cm broad. The leaves are dark green, leathery, shiny, (5–)10–25(–30) cm long and 4–10 cm broad, with a finely serrated margin.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Plant Image Library, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Chinese Elm
cards.subtitle: Ulmus parvifolia
cards.description: Ulmus parvifolia, the Chinese elm or lacebark elm, is a species of flowering plant native to eastern Asia, including China, India, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Siberia, and Kazakhstan. It has been described as "one of the most splendid elms, having the poise of a graceful Nothofagus".
cards.keyFeatures: A small to medium deciduous or semideciduous (rarely semievergreen) tree, it grows to 10–18 m (33–59 ft) tall and 15–20 m (49–66 ft) wide, with a slender trunk and crown. The leathery, lustrous green, single-toothed leaves are small, 2–5 cm long by 1–3 cm broad, and often are retained as late as December or even January in Europe and North America.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Reid Hardin, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Reid Hardin

cards.name: Hoop Pine
cards.subtitle: Araucaria cunninghamii
cards.description: Araucaria cunninghamii is a species of conifer in the family Araucariaceae, known as hoop pine. Other less commonly used names include colonial pine, Queensland pine, Dorrigo pine, Moreton Bay pine and Richmond River pine. The scientific name honours the botanist and explorer Allan Cunningham, who collected the first specimens in the 1820s.
cards.keyFeatures: The leaves on young trees are awl-shaped, 1–2 cm long, about 2 mm thick at the base, and scale-like, incurved, 1–2 cm long and 4 mm broad on mature trees. The cones are ovoid, 8–10 cm long and 6–8 cm diameter, and take about 18 months to mature.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Shaun Swanepoel, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Shaun Swanepoel

cards.name: Bell-fruited Mallee
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus preissiana
cards.description: Eucalyptus preissiana, commonly known as bell-fruited mallee, is a species of small tree or shrub that occurs in an area between Albany and Esperance in Western Australia. It has a spreading habit, smooth bark, elliptical to egg-shaped or oblong leaves, flower buds in groups of three, yellow flowers and cup-shaped, conical or bell-shaped fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus preissiana is a mallee that typically grows to a height of 3–5 m (9.8–16.4 ft) with a sprawling habit, and forms a lignotuber. It has smooth, greyish and brown bark.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Salicyna, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Deodar Cedar
cards.subtitle: Cedrus deodara
cards.description: Cedrus deodara, the deodar cedar, Himalayan cedar, or deodar, is a species of cedar, a conifer in the pine family, Pinaceae, native to the Himalayas.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a large coniferous tree reaching 40–50 metres (131–164 feet) tall, exceptionally 60 m (197 ft) with a trunk up to 3 m (10 ft) in diameter. It has a conic crown with level branches and drooping branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dinesh Valke, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Bangalay
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus botryoides
cards.description: Eucalyptus botryoides, commonly known as the bangalay, bastard jarrah, woollybutt or southern mahogany, is a small to tall tree native to southeastern Australia. Reaching up to 40 metres (130 feet) high, it has rough bark on its trunk and branches. It is found on sandstone- or shale-based soils in open woodland, or on more sandy soils behind sand dunes.
cards.keyFeatures: In favourable conditions, Eucalyptus botryoides can grow as a straight-trunked tree to 40 m (130 ft) high with a dbh of 1 m (3.3 ft), although it is often shorter in poorer situations.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Max Campbell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Max Campbell

cards.name: Elephant Bush
cards.subtitle: Portulacaria afra
cards.description: Portulacaria afra (known as elephant bush, porkbush, purslane tree, dwarf jade and spekboom in Afrikaans) is a small-leaved succulent plant found in South Africa. These succulents commonly have a reddish stem and green leaves, but a variegated cultivar is often seen in cultivation. They are simple to care for and make easy houseplants for a sunny location.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a soft-wooded, semi-evergreen upright shrub or small tree, usually 2.5–4.5 metres (8–15 ft) tall. P. afra has smaller and rounder pads and more compact growth (shorter internodal spaces, down to 1.5 millimetres (0.059 in)).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Shaun Swanepoel, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Shaun Swanepoel

cards.name: Karo
cards.subtitle: Pittosporum crassifolium
cards.description: Pittosporum crassifolium, karo, stiffleaf cheesewood, kaikaro or kihiki is a relatively fast-growing large shrub or small tree with an erect, fastigiate growth habit. It is endemic to New Zealand. This species is self-supporting with a simple form that can grow up to 10 m tall.
cards.keyFeatures: The leaves on this species are approximately 5-10x2-3cm and are oval shaped, dark green and leathery with grey tomentum (fine hairs) on the undersides of the leaves including the petioles and inflorescences.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jenny Christianson

cards.name: English Oak
cards.subtitle: Quercus robur
cards.description: Quercus robur, pedunculate oak, European oak, or English oak, is a species of flowering plant in the beech and oak family, Fagaceae. It is a large tree, native to Europe and western Asia, and is widely cultivated in other temperate regions.
cards.keyFeatures: Pedunculate oak is a deciduous tree, typically maturing at up to 20 m in height, and sometimes up to 40 metres (130 ft), with a single stout trunk typically reaching up to 4 m, sometimes exceeding 10 m (33 ft) in girth (circumference at breast height), or even reportedly 14 m in pollarded specimens.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Stephen James McWilliam

cards.name: Tree-of-heaven
cards.subtitle: Ailanthus altissima
cards.description: Ailanthus altissima ( ay-LAN-thəss al-TIH-sim-ə), commonly known as tree of heaven or ailanthus tree, is a deciduous tree in the quassia family. It is native to northeast, central China, and Taiwan. Unlike other members of the genus Ailanthus, it is found in temperate climates rather than the tropics.
cards.keyFeatures: Ailanthus altissima is a medium-sized tree that reaches heights between 17 and 27 m (60 and 90 ft) with a diameter at breast height of about 1 m (3 ft). The bark is smooth and light grey, often becoming somewhat rougher with light tan fissures as the tree ages.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Native Willow
cards.subtitle: Callistachys lanceolata
cards.description: Callistachys lanceolata, commonly known as the wonnich, native willow, or greenbush is the sole species in the genus Callistachys. It is a species of erect shrub or small tree that is native to the south-west of Western Australia and is naturalised in some other Australian states.
cards.keyFeatures: Callistachys lanceolata is an erect evergreen tree or shrub that typically grows to a height of 1.5–7 m (4 ft 11 in – 23 ft 0 in) and has silky-hairy young stems. The plant has conspicuous and attractive inflorescence composed of racemes with yellow flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leon Perrie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Leon Perrie

cards.name: Japanese Maple
cards.subtitle: Acer palmatum
cards.description: Acer palmatum, commonly known as Japanese maple, palmate maple, or smooth Japanese maple (Korean: danpungnamu [단풍나무]; Japanese: irohamomiji [イロハモミジ] or momiji [紅葉]), is a species of woody plant native to Korea, Japan, China, eastern Mongolia, and far eastern Russia.
cards.keyFeatures: Acer palmatum is deciduous, with the growth habit of a shrub or small tree reaching heights of 6 to 10 m (20 to 33 ft), rarely 16 m (52 ft), reaching a mature width of 4.5 to 10 m (15 to 33 ft), often growing as an understory plant in shady woodlands in its native habitat. It may have multiple trunks joining close to the ground.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Katja Schulz, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bower Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia cognata
cards.description: Acacia cognata, commonly known as bower wattle, river wattle or narrow-leaf bower-wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is an erect or spreading shrub or tree with willowly and arching branchlets, narrowly linear phyllodes, spherical heads of pale lemon-yellow flowers and linear, papery, glabrous, pods.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia cognata is an erect or spreading shrub or tree that typically grows to a height of 3–10 m (9.8–32.8 ft) and is often sticky. Its branchlets are usually glabrous, willowy and arching.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Tree Aeonium
cards.subtitle: Aeonium arboreum
cards.description: Aeonium arboreum, the tree aeonium, tree houseleek, or Irish rose, is a succulent, subtropical subshrub in the flowering plant family Crassulaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Aeonium arboreum grows as a less branched subshrub and reaches stature heights of up to 2 metres. The more or less upright or ascending, smooth, not net-like patterned stem axes have a diameter of 1 to 3 centimetres.
cards.imageCredit: (c) William Stephens, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by William Stephens

cards.name: Peach
cards.subtitle: Prunus persica
cards.description: The peach (Prunus persica) is a deciduous tree that bears edible juicy fruits with various characteristics. Most are simply called peaches, while the glossy-skinned, non-fuzzy varieties are called nectarines. Though from the same species, they are regarded commercially as different fruits.
cards.keyFeatures: The peach is a deciduous tree or tree like shrub that may rarely grow to as much as 10 meters (33 ft) tall, but is more typically 3 m (10 ft) with large specimens reaching 4 m (13 ft). The spread of the crown is similar to the height, ranging from 3 to 4 m (9.8 to 13.1 ft).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Yair Haklai, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Argyle Apple
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus cinerea
cards.description: Eucalyptus cinerea, commonly known as the Argyle apple, mealy stringbark or silver dollar tree, is a species of small- to medium-sized tree that is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has rough, fibrous bark on the trunk and branches, usually only juvenile, glaucous, egg-shaped evergreen leaves, flower buds in groups of three, white flowers and conical to bell-shaped fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus cinerea is a tree that typically grows to a height of 15–30 m (49–98 ft) tall and forms a lignotuber. It has thick, fibrous, reddish brown to grey brown, longitudinally fissured bark on the trunk to the small branches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dilrukshan Priyantha Wijesinghe, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Hillock Bush
cards.subtitle: Melaleuca hypericifolia
cards.description: Melaleuca hypericifolia, commonly known as hillock bush, is a plant in the myrtle family, Myrtaceae, genus Melaleuca and is endemic to New South Wales in Australia. It has large, orange to red flower spikes and consequently is a commonly cultivated species. In 1797, James Edward Smith described the plant as: "The most beautiful of the genus.
cards.keyFeatures: Melaleuca hypericifolia is a large woody shrub or small tree growing to 6 m (20 ft) in height, with greyish papery bark. Its leaves are arranged in alternate pairs (decussate), 10–40 mm (0.4–2 in) long, 4–10 mm (0.2–0.4 in) wide, narrow elliptic in shape with a central groove on the upper surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Diana Studer, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Diana Studer

cards.name: Brown Stringybark
cards.subtitle: Eucalyptus baxteri
cards.description: Eucalyptus baxteri, commonly known as brown stringybark, is a medium-sized tree that is endemic to the south-east of mainland Australia. It has rough, stringy bark to the thinnest branches, lance-shaped or curved adult leaves, green to yellow flower buds in groups of between nine and fifteen, and cup-shaped or hemispherical fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Eucalyptus baxteri is a tree that grows to a height of 40 metres (131 ft) and forms a lignotuber. It has grey to brownish, stringy or fibrous bark from the trunk to the thinnest branches.

cards.name: Lilly Pilly
cards.subtitle: Syzygium smithii
cards.description: Syzygium smithii (formerly Acmena smithii) is a summer-flowering, winter-fruiting evergreen tree native to Australia that belongs to the myrtle family, Myrtaceae. It shares the common name "lilly pilly" with several other plants. It is planted as shrubs or hedgerows, and features: rough, woody bark; cream and green smooth, waxy leaves; flushes of pink new growth; and white to maroon edible berries.
cards.keyFeatures: Syzygium smithii grows as a tree to 20 m (66 ft) high by 5–15 m (16–49 ft) wide, with a trunk attaining a diameter of 70 cm (2.3 ft). The largest tree was recorded at Dingo Creek Flora Reserve, south of Tenterfield, being 30 m (98 ft) tall and a trunk 60 cm (2.0 ft) wide.

cards.name: Pomegranate
cards.subtitle: Punica granatum
cards.description: The pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub or tree in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5–5 metres (5–16 ft) tall.
cards.keyFeatures: The pomegranate is a shrub or small tree growing 1.5 to 5 m (5 to 16 ft) high, with multiple spiny branches. It is long-lived, with some specimens in France surviving for 200 years.

cards.name: Osage-orange
cards.subtitle: Maclura pomifera
cards.description: Maclura pomifera, commonly known as the Osage orange ( OH-sayj), is a small deciduous tree or large shrub, native to the south-central United States. It is a member of the mulberry family, Moraceae. It typically grows about 8 to 15 m (30–50 ft) tall.

cards.name: Bay Laurel
cards.subtitle: Laurus nobilis
cards.description: Laurus nobilis () is an aromatic evergreen tree or large shrub with green, glabrous (smooth) leaves. Common names include bay tree (especially in the United Kingdom), bay laurel, sweet bay, true laurel, Grecian laurel, or simply laurel. It is in the flowering plant family Lauraceae.
cards.keyFeatures: The laurel is an evergreen shrub or small tree, variable in size and sometimes reaching 7–18 m (23–59 ft) tall. The genus Laurus includes three accepted species, whose diagnostic key characters often overlap.

cards.name: Tea Tree
cards.subtitle: Leptospermum scoparium
cards.description: Mānuka (Māori pronunciation: [ˈmaːnʉka]; Leptospermum scoparium) is a species of flowering plant in the myrtle family Myrtaceae, native to New Zealand (including the Chatham Islands) and south-east Australia. Bees produce mānuka honey from its nectar.
cards.keyFeatures: Mānuka is a prolific shrub-type tree and is often one of the first species to regenerate on cleared land. It is typically a shrub growing to 2–5 m (7–16 ft) tall, but can grow into a moderately sized tree, up to 15 m (49 ft) or so in height.

cards.name: Black Locust
cards.subtitle: Robinia pseudoacacia
cards.description: Robinia pseudoacacia, commonly known as black locust, is a medium-sized hardwood deciduous tree, belonging to the tribe Robinieae of the legume family. Another common name is false acacia, a literal translation of the specific name (pseudo [Greek ψευδο-] meaning 'fake' or 'false' and acacia referring to the genus of plants with the same name).
cards.keyFeatures: The roots of black locust contain nodules that allow it to fix nitrogen, as is common within the pea family. Trees reach a typical height of 12–30 metres (40–100 feet) with a diameter of 0.6–1.2 m (2–4 ft).

cards.name: Snow-in-Summer
cards.subtitle: Melaleuca linariifolia
cards.description: Melaleuca linariifolia is a plant in the myrtle family Myrtaceae, and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is commonly known as snow-in-summer, narrow-leaved paperbark, flax-leaved paperbark and in the language of the Gadigal people as budjur. A hardy plant, it flowers prolifically in late spring or summer, making it a popular garden shrub or small tree in temperate places.
cards.keyFeatures: Melaleuca linariifolia is a small tree growing to a height of 6–10 m (20–30 ft) with distinctive and attractive white or creamy white, papery bark and a dense canopy.
